title: Compliance Head & MLRO, Pakistan
description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced, commercially aware, and regulatory-savvy compliance professional to join us as Head of Compliance and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO).
The role will be instrumental in building the compliance programme from the ground up, and embedding a culture of compliance across the organisation.
Broader team management responsibilities will be added in due course for regulatory strategy, operational execution, and governance.
 
 

What You’ll Be Doing

Regulatory Engagement

  • Serve as the primary point of contact with relevant regulatory bodies.
  • Ensure the organisation meets all applicable governance requirements, including fit and proper obligations for Approved and Designated Persons.
  • Monitor and interpret regulatory developments relevant to virtual assets, and advise senior management and the Board accordingly.

Compliance Programme Development & Management

  • Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive compliance framework aligned with local requirements, FATF recommendations, and international best practice for virtual asset service providers (VASPs).
  • Develop, review, and update all internal policies and procedures covering AML/CFT, KYC, customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, data protection, cybersecurity compliance, and safeguarding of client assets.
  • Establish and oversee the compliance monitoring programme, including periodic testing, gap analysis, and reporting to senior management and the Board.
  • Prepare and present regular compliance reports to the Board and relevant committees, including on regulatory changes, compliance breaches, and remediation progress.
  • Ensure compliance considerations are integrated into new product design and operations from the inception phase by driving solutions that balance commercial outcomes and innovation, while maintaining a robust compliance posture using a clear risk-based approach.
  • Review technical documentation, user journeys, and product flows to ensure compliance risks are addressed; provide clear, actionable and solution-focused advice during the product lifecycle.
  • Build and scale compliance policies governing advertising, social media campaigns, influencer partnerships, and product launches.
  • Partner with Legal, Product, and Marketing teams to operationalize a timely review process for client-facing assets and go-to-market materials.

AML/CFT & MLRO Duties

  • Act as the designated MLRO, with full statutory responsibility for overseeing the organisation's AML/CFT framework.
  • Receive, review, and assess all internal Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from staff, and make informed decisions on whether to file external disclosures with competent local authorities.
  • Oversee and continuously improve the transaction monitoring programme, with support from global compliance and product functions.
  • Ensure robust sanctions screening against all applicable lists, including OFAC, UK OFSI, UN, EU, and applicable local sanctions designations.
  • Oversee customer risk scoring, risk-based KYC/CDD processes, and enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers, politically exposed persons (PEPs), and customers from high-risk jurisdictions.

Governance & Culture

  • Act as a key member of the senior leadership team, providing compliance input on new products, services, partnerships, and business initiatives.
  • Champion a strong compliance culture across the organisation through training, communications, and leadership by example.
  • Design and deliver AML/CFT and compliance training programmes for all staff, ensuring completion records are maintained.
  • Ensure that the organisation's compliance obligations are adequately resourced, and advise the Board on staffing, systems, and budget requirements.
  • Establish and maintain a compliance manual, risk register and oversee the escalation and resolution of compliance incidents and breaches.

Reporting & Recordkeeping

  • Prepare and submit all required regulatory reports and notifications to relevant authorities within stipulated deadlines.
  • Ensure that all compliance records, SAR documentation, KYC files, and transaction monitoring records are maintained in accordance with applicable retention requirements.
  • Support and facilitate any inspections, supervisory visits, or regulatory examinations.
 

What We Look For In You

  • Qualifications

    • Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Business, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is advantageous.
    • Professional certification in compliance or AML is strongly preferred (e.g. CAMS, ICA Certificate/Diploma in AML or Compliance, CFE, or equivalent).

    Experience

    • Minimum of 8 years of experience in compliance, AML, or financial crime prevention, with at least 3 years in a senior or leadership compliance role.
    • Demonstrated in-house experience working within virtual asset service providers (VASPs), cryptocurrency exchanges, fintech firms, or regulated financial institutions.
    • Prior experience as an MLRO or Deputy MLRO is highly desirable.
    • Experience engaging directly with financial regulators and the financial intelligence unit
    • Hands-on experience building compliance programmes from the ground up in a start-up or scaling environment is a significant advantage.
    • Familiarity with the regional regulatory framework and requirements is strongly preferred.

    Knowledge & Skills

    • Deep understanding of FATF Recommendations and their application to virtual asset service providers, including the Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16)
    • Strong knowledge of crypto-specific AML typologies.
    • Proficiency with blockchain analytics and transaction monitoring tools (e.g. Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM Labs, or equivalent).
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Urdu.
    • Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify and articulate complex risk scenarios clearly.
    • Demonstrated ability to engage constructively with regulators, external auditors, and law enforcement.
    • High degree of personal integrity and sound professional judgment.
 

Nice to Haves

    • Experience in cryptocurrency or blockchain compliance programs.
    • Experience working in a multi-national financial institution setting.
    • Familiarity with compliance technology and analytics tools.
    • Prior exposure to multi-jurisdictional compliance oversight.
    • In-depth knowledge of crypto products, including spot trading, derivatives, staking, lending/borrowing, DeFi, and stablecoins.
 

Additional Notes

This role will be subject to fit and proper assessment as part of the licensing process. Candidates must be prepared to undergo background checks, provide regulatory questionnaires, CVs, references, and proof of relevant qualifications. Prior enforcement history, regulatory sanctions, or unexplained gaps in professional record may affect eligibility.

 

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

title: Onboarding Manager
description:
BitGo is the leading infrastructure provider of digital asset solutions, delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since our founding in 2013, we have focused on enabling our clients to securely navigate the digital asset space. With a global presence and multiple Trust companies, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of retail investors worldwide. As the operational backbone of the digital economy, BitGo handles a significant portion of Bitcoin network transactions and is the largest independent digital asset custodian, and staking provider, in the world. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Onboarding Manager to own and drive BitGo’s client onboarding function for our MAS-regulated Singapore entity. Reporting to BitGo’s APAC Managing Director, this role will own the end-end client lifecycle; including client onboarding, ongoing due diligence, periodic reviews and off-boarding.

This is a player/coach role where you will manage and mentor an Onboarding Associate while remaining deeply hands-on in day-to-day execution. You will own and manage onboarding cases directly, and help establish strong operating standards across the function. You will have the opportunity to shape BitGo Singapore’s onboarding operating model as the business continues to scale.

The ideal candidate combines strong KYC/KYB expertise and a solid understanding of MAS regulatory requirements paired with commercial and operational judgement. You are resourceful, pragmatic, and creative in solving problems, comfortable owning complex cases end to end, and able to find practical ways forward when the path is not always clear. You partner effectively with cross-functional stakeholders, challenge inefficient ways of working, and thrive in a fast-moving environment.

Responsibilities

Client Onboarding and Offboarding

  • Review and progress onboarding applications end to end, ensuring high execution quality, robust documentation and timely completion
  • Manage onboarding queues and priorities to maintain strong throughput and adherence to service level expectations
  • Identify information gaps and manage requests for information efficiently to minimize unnecessary client friction
  • Partner closely with Compliance on cases requiring additional review or escalation
  • Own client offboarding end to end, including sanctions and risk driven terminations, dormant and inactive account closures, and coordination of account wind-down with Operations and Compliance
  • Draft and manage client-facing exit communications, ensuring exits are executed cleanly, defensibly, and with appropriate documentation and record retention

Stakeholder Management

  • Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Operations, Compliance, and other cross-functional stakeholders to move clients through onboarding effectively
  • Communicate onboarding requirements and blockers clearly to internal stakeholders and help drive cases toward resolution

title: Deputy General Counsel - Litigation & Investigations, Asia Pacific, Middle East & Africa
description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Team

The Global Legal team provides legal advice and guidance to OKX and its affiliated entities across all coverage areas and geographic locations, and supports business growth by working with all teams within the company to help them achieve their goals. Our team has attorneys around the world, and handles legal matters in literally hundreds of countries across the globe.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Criminal referrals, law enforcement and prosecution support:
    • Own OKX’s framework for identifying conduct that warrants criminal referral and work directly with relevant authorities to follow-through on charging and prosecution.
    • Working closely with teams in Risk and Compliance, build and package referral files to an acceptable prosecutorial standard.
    • Drive referred matters through to charge and prosecution.
    • Serve as the senior legal relationship owner for police and prosecutors and develop and maintain relationships throughout the region.
  • Civil litigation:
    • Own and lead the regional civil docket end-to-end including intake, early case assessment, strategy and resolution both on the defence and plaintiff side.
    • Lead the affirmative side of civil disputes, e.g., recovery actions, injunctions, disclosure applications, applications against counterparties, service providers, bad actors, etc.
    • Assess and develop strategy for defensive civil claims including consumer claims at volume, market conduct issues, and coordinate on relevant contentious employment matters.
    • Manage and lead commercial disputes.
  • Arbitration
    • Real depth of arbitration experience preferred. Lead OKX’s arbitrations in the region as counsel-in-charge, including pleadings, document production, witness and expert evidence, hearings, enforcement proceedings.
    • Assess mass arbitration exposure in conjunction with business priorities and develop strategic plan for risk mitigation.
    • Advise business and business Legal teams on dispute resolution clauses.
  • Regulatory Enforcement & Internal Investigations
    • Develop strategy and lead OKX’s response to regulatory enforcement inquiries working in close collaboration with Global Regulatory Legal team.
    • Scope, lead and where appropriate personally conduct sensitive internal investigations. Deliver as needed root causes analysis and collaborate cross-functionally on remediation.
  • Team leadership: Lead and develop the in-region team, embed AI to drive efficiency, and partner across Legal, Compliance, Risk, Finance, HR and Communications.
  • External counsel, budget and reporting: Select and manage external counsel and experts; own the regional contentious budget and in-house/outside counsel decisions; ensure proper matter tracking and disclosure; deliver decision-ready reporting to the Global Head and governance forums.

What We Look For In You

  • Admitted as solicitor or barrister in Hong Kong or Singapore
  • 12+ years post-qualification experience in contentious work, with Asia experience. More experienced candidates will be considered.
  • Prosecutorial or criminal enforcement background (prosecutor, government trial lawyer, or criminal/regulatory enforcement counsel), plus arbitration and trial experience and a track record leading a team. Prior in-house experience preferred.
  • Sound judgment under ambiguity; able to operate in a fast-paced environment with a growing regulatory landscape.
  • Fluent written and spoken English. Mandarin and/or Cantonese at professional working level strongly preferred — a material advantage for law enforcement and regulatory engagement in the region.
  • Willing to travel across the region.

Nice to Haves

  • Additional qualification in England & Wales, New York, California, Texas, Australia, or another common law jurisdiction welcome.
  • Experience in crypto, digital assets, fintech, traditional finance, or payments.
  • Experience or familiarity with Middle East disputes and enforcement.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!
 
 
Please note that Hong Kong is a group-level service hub, and OKX does not carry on a business of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong.

title: Senior Financial Crimes Compliance Controls Strategist
description:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking its first dedicated Financial Crimes Compliance Controls Senior Strategist to build and own the framework that demonstrates FCC controls are working as intended, remain effective as risk evolves, and can be clearly supported in bank-partner, audit, and regulatory examinations.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the intersection of financial-crimes compliance, controls effectiveness, technology, data, and AI-enabled operations. You will own FCC’s approach to testing, documenting, and improving manual and automated controls, including procedures, detection rules, AI and LLM-enabled workflows, and automation deployments.

You will serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for program-level Product, Engineering, Design, and Data (“PEDD”) initiatives, ensuring FCC requirements, controls, and risk considerations are incorporated into strategic product and technology planning. This role complements the broader team’s cross-functional partnerships by focusing specifically on major PEDD-led initiatives.

This is a builder role for an experienced financial-crimes compliance professional with deep analytical skills and strong BSA/AML, and sanctions subject-matter expertise You will assess emerging and existing financial-crimes risks, make sound and defensible control decisions, and help build the processes, technology partnerships, and governance needed for FCC to scale responsibly. You will not simply maintain existing processes. You will help shape how FCC’s controls environment, AI strategy, and product partnership model evolve.

What You’ll Do

  • Own FCC’s controls-effectiveness across manual procedures, detection rules, workflow controls, automation deployments, and AI or LLM-enabled capabilities.

  • Establish standards for testing, evidence retention, issue identification, remediation tracking, and ongoing control monitoring.

  • Serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for major PEDD-led initiatives, defining FCC requirements and ensuring compliance needs are incorporated into product and technology planning.

  • Partner with PEDD to translate financial-crimes requirements into scalable workflows, controls, and user experiences.

  • Own FCC’s internal AI and automation strategy, including identifying high-value use cases and ensuring AI-enabled workflows are appropriately tested, documented, monitored, and supported by appropriate human oversight.

  • Use financial crimes domain expertise, data, and analytical methods to proactively evaluate risk coverage, identify emerging risks or control gaps, and drive solutions and improvements..

  • Serve as an independent, qualified secondary reviewer for FCC compliance reviews where segregation of duties or heightened review is required.

What You Need

  • 7+ years of experience in financial-crimes compliance, AML/BSA or sanctions.

  • At least 3 years of experience in a technical compliance, controls, compliance-testing, quality-assurance, or similar role.

  • At least 3 years of experience as an AML or financial-crimes trusted advisor, including partnering with technical, operational, product, or business stakeholders on risk-based controls and decisions.

  • Experience developing, implementing, or evaluating controls across both manual and technology-enabled processes.

  • Deep understanding of financial-crimes typologies and how risk evolves across products, payment flows, customer types, and operational processes.

  • AI fluency, including the ability to independently use approved AI tools, critically assess output quality and limitations, and lead strategic AI and automation initiatives within a compliance environment.

  • Strong data-analysis skills sufficient to assess control performance, evaluate AI or LLM-enabled controls, identify trends or gaps, and partner credibly with technical teams.

  • Experience presenting testing results, control documentation, risk findings, or program materials to regulators, examiners, auditors, or bank partners.

  • ACAMS certification or equivalent financial-crimes certification.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex compliance requirements and risk decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Comfort operating with significant autonomy and building structure in a new, evolving role.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience evaluating or implementing AI, machine learning, LLM, automation, or decisioning controls in a regulated environment.

  • Experience supporting a fintech, payments, banking, card, or money-transmission compliance program.

  • Experience designing controls for transaction monitoring, KYC or KYB, EDD, sanctions screening, suspicious-activity reporting, or payment-risk workflows.

title: Senior Product Manager, Trading
description:
COMPANY

At 0x, our mission is to "Create a Tokenized World Where All Forms of Value Can Flow Freely". We deliver this to web3 builders with a delightfully simple suite of developer APIs that provide faster trading, better prices, and superior user experience.

Founded in 2017, we’ve processed over 211M+ transactions and $180B+ in trading volume from users trading on Matcha, Coinbase Wallet, Robinhood Wallet, Phantom, Rainbow, DefiLlama, MetaMask, Zerion, Zapper, and many more. Our investors include Greylock Partners, Pantera Capital, and Jump Crypto.

When you join 0x, you’ll become part of a veteran team of crypto builders who know the importance of code quality, team cohesion, and a culture of learning.


About the role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to work directly with our CEO across our suite of trading APIs and new product initiatives. This is a hands-on IC role on a lean product team. You'll be deep in the data, close to customers, and working alongside engineers from concept through to launch.

This suits a strategic operator with a founder mentality. You take ownership, default to action, and drive things end to end without waiting for explicit instructions. When the data is incomplete, you form a thesis and validate it with prototypes, fast experiments, and tight iterations.

What you'll do

  • Own strategy and roadmap for your product area - an existing set of our trading APIs or a net-new initiative

  • Form your product ideas and decisions from three independent sources, not one:

    • What customers tell you. Have regular check-ins with them, analyze their metrics, understand their pain points and what they're building next

    • What customers can’t tell you. Dig into onchain and internal data to spot gaps in our performance, shifts in the competitive landscape, and emerging opportunities

    • What you see yourself. You're plugged into DeFi and active in trading communities. You know firsthand what works and what doesn't

  • Be a true partner to our engineering leads - reason through hard problems with them, weigh the tradeoffs, and decide what's worth building

  • Partner with GTM on positioning and driving adoption

  • Work directly with the CEO and leadership to help shape product direction

Who you are

  • 6+ years in product, or the equivalent as a founder, GM, or trader who moved into building

  • Shipped B2B, API, or infra products with real adoption and revenue

  • Data-driven - you build your own Dune dashboards and dig into API performance and internal analytics in Grafana, Metabase, or similar

  • Technically fluent - you hold your own with engineers on routing, execution quality, latency, and whatever else the problem demands

  • DeFi-native - onchain trading, perps, dex aggregation. You're the user you're building for

  • Expert AI user - you run agents, automate your workflows, and build tooling that multiplies your output

  • You exhibit our core values: do the right thing, consistently ship, and focus on long-term impact

Preferred

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

 

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.

Location

  • Remote – Europe or US (EST only)

  • Hybrid – Paris or New York

 

Role

Morpho's GTM motion has grown faster than the operations behind it. Pipeline visibility, CRM hygiene, forecasting, and tooling are split across people who all have other jobs, and nobody owns the end-to-end picture. This role owns RevOps outright and builds the systems that help the GTM team close more relevant deals, faster, working directly within the Business Operations team, directly under the Head of BizOps.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own GTM dashboards and KPI reporting so the team tracks what matters and trusts the numbers.

  • Run the GTM tech stack, automations, and AI tooling to keep business developers fast and well informed.

  • Keep the CRM minimal and clean, with stages, hygiene, and processes people actually follow.

  • Build business intelligence and forecasting to set targets that are ambitious and credible, and to spot new trends early.

  • Surface signals from markets and media so business developers can chase, upsell, and close at the right moment.

  • Partner with GTM leadership and Finance on comp design, quota setting, and territory assignment.

  • Own the knowledge base and data management so accurate information is easy to find and reuse.

 

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days

  • You are fully up to speed on the Morpho product, protocol, and roadmap, and you understand how the GTM team operates today.

  • You have a prioritized plan for what to build, fix, and delete, and you are already making reps faster.

 

First 3 months

  • You have fixed the biggest gaps and bottlenecks: a cleaner CRM, simpler processes, and the automations, dashboards, and forecasts business developers rely on daily.

  • You are central to productivity assessment, rep attribution, and deal tracking.

 

First 6 months

  • You own the full RevOps stack and bridge GTM and Finance.

  • Leadership has full visibility into the business to make better decisions, and you lead entire projects end to end.

 

Must Have Skills & Experience

  • DeFi native: you use onchain products and understand how protocols and their users behave.

  • Experience as a RevOps, growth engineer, or business analyst at a B2B startup.

  • Tech or software background: comfortable building automations and reasoning about connected systems.

  • Strong with data: cleaning, modeling, analyzing, and reporting it accurately.

  • Finance experience

  • Business mindset with a critical eye: you challenge metrics and simplify by default.

  • Strong ownership and autonomy: doesn't wait to be told.

  • Clear and crisp async communication.

  • Comfort operating in fast-changing, ambiguous contexts.

  • Team-first mindset, low ego.

Perks & Benefits

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

 

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.

title: GTM Senior Business Systems Analyst
description:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is in a critical phase of growth. We grew immensely last year and are building out a talented business systems team to ensure we maintain this trajectory for years to come. You’ll work directly with our Sales, Account Management, Partnerships, and Product teams to execute mission-critical business systems projects across the organization. What You'll Do

title: Client Associate
description:
About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

Polymarket is reinventing what it means to know your customers — and our goal is simple: make every trader feel like they have a person, not a portal. Client Associates are not ticket-closers. They're the human side of the platform. You'll get new traders oriented, answer the questions that actually matter, and be the name customers recognize when they need something — from their first market to becoming confident, experienced users.

This role is for someone who genuinely cares about the people on the other end of every conversation and takes it personally when a customer has a bad time. You don't need a trading background, but you're curious about markets, quick to learn a technical product, and comfortable explaining it in plain language. You'll act as a mini-founder for your customer relationships, accountable for the experience and not just the inbox.

What You'll Do

  • Be the person your customers know by name — when they have a question about markets, positions, or the platform, you're the one who answers it clearly, fast, and without escalating the routine stuff

  • Guide customers through onboarding, from their first market to trading with confidence; if they don't understand how something works, that's yours to fix

  • Keep customer communication consistent, clear, and human — no one should ever have to read your message twice

  • Know when a customer's needs go beyond the scope of the role and get them to the right person without dropping the thread

  • Spot recurring questions and friction points, then bring clear, actionable recommendations back to the team and build simple, repeatable processes others can pick up without a long explanation

What We're Looking For

  • At least 1 year of client-facing experience, account management, or a role where you were directly responsible for relationships with external users or customers

  • Strong written communication skills — you write clearly, get to the point, and don't make clients read the same message twice

  • Comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy — you don't wait to be told what to follow up on

  • Organized enough to ensure nothing falls through the cracks

  • Able to learn a technical product quickly and explain it in plain language to someone who has never used it before

  • (Plus) Familiarity with prediction markets, futures, or other derivatives products

  • (Plus) Experience building or improving a client-facing process from scratch, not just inheriting one

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

description:
About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

Institutional capital is one of the most important vectors for Polymarket. Market-makers, hedge funds, trading desks, and sophisticated financial players are paying close attention — and we need someone to own the full process of bringing them onto the platform. This role sits within Operations, reports directly to senior leadership, and leads the institutional onboarding function end to end.

The work is operational and relational in equal measure. You'll design and run the onboarding process for institutional counterparties, work closely with legal and compliance to keep things moving, and be the face of Polymarket to some of the most sophisticated traders in the world. Every week an institution is stuck in onboarding is a week they're not trading.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end institutional onboarding process, from initial outreach and documentation collection through account activation and first trade

  • Design and implement scalable onboarding workflows that reduce time-to-live for new institutional accounts without sacrificing compliance requirements

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for institutional clients during onboarding, setting clear expectations and keeping deals moving

  • Coordinate with legal, compliance, and product teams to resolve blockers, negotiate documentation requirements, and ensure institutional accounts meet all necessary standards

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of institutional prospects moving through onboarding, and report on status, conversion rates, and bottlenecks to leadership

  • Identify patterns in where onboarding slows down and fix them — whether that means updating internal processes, improving documentation, or escalating product gaps

  • Work with the broader operations and growth teams to define what institutional success looks like post-onboarding and ensure a clean handoff

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in financial services, with meaningful time spent in client onboarding, institutional sales support, or operations at a bank, brokerage, exchange, or fintech

  • Deep familiarity with KYC, KYB, and AML processes and the ability to navigate them without constant hand-holding from legal or compliance

  • Proven track record of owning a client-facing process end-to-end, not just executing tasks within someone else's system

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple institutional onboardings simultaneously without anything falling through the cracks

  • Comfortable working in ambiguity — this role requires building structure where little exists today

  • Clear, direct communicator who can represent Polymarket credibly to sophisticated financial counterparties

  • (Plus) Experience at a crypto exchange, prediction market, or other alternative trading platform

  • (Plus) Familiarity with CFTC-regulated entities and the documentation requirements specific to derivatives or swaps trading

  • (Plus) Experience hiring and managing a small operations or onboarding team

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

Head of Fraud, Payments & Banking
description:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

As Head of Fraud, Payments & Banking, you'll own the strategy, governance, and day-to-day execution of Kraken's payments and banking fraud prevention programs, from front-line detection and analyst operations through policy design and executive reporting. This role carries a strong mandate to bring a consistent global coverage lens across all markets — ensuring fraud controls, payments oversight, and banking risk programs meet the highest regulatory bar across every jurisdiction we operate in.

The opportunity

  • Own the end-to-end payments and banking fraud prevention strategy across all Kraken products, setting the vision, roadmap, and OKRs in collaboration with Product, Engineering, Security, Compliance, and Legal

  • Build, lead, and mentor a multi-tiered fraud organization — analysts, investigators, and managers — establishing career progression frameworks with clear advancement criteria

  • Work closely with the Executive Team and regulators to stay ahead of emerging fraud trends, techniques, and technologies across the payments and banking industry, directing in-depth analysis to proactively identify and close vulnerabilities

  • Monitor payment trends and regulatory shifts, identifying opportunities to optimize approval/decline rates and revenue while maintaining fraud discipline

  • Design, implement, and maintain payments and banking fraud policies, rule frameworks, and control processes across all products

  • Maintain Risk assessment, mitigation, Governance and Audit controls

  • Lead comprehensive risk assessments and implement preventive controls that support governance, audit, and regulatory requirements

  • Oversee payments and banking fraud detection systems and tools, and own escalation pathways for complex or novel fraud cases in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and Customer Support

  • Ensure the analyst team maintains SLA and QA standards across high-volume, real-time alert queues

  • Serve as the primary point of coordination between payments and banking Fraud Operations and Customer Support, Compliance, Legal, Product, and Security

  • Direct data analysis and reporting on fraud and payment KPIs, delivering clear, actionable reporting on a daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadence to executive leadership

  • Apply a consistent global coverage standard across all markets, ensuring they are proactively tracked and embedded into policy rather than addressed reactively

What you bring

  • 10+ years of experience in banking, payment processing, or fraud risk management, including experience building or leading a fraud team

  • Demonstrated experience managing both strategic fraud/payments programs and front-line, high-volume analyst operations

  • Proven track record with Card, Third-Party, and Peer-to-Peer payment fraud, along with relevant banking regulatory and compliance frameworks

  • Working knowledge of UK and other non-US regulatory regimes (e.g., FCA, PSR) relevant to fraud, payments, and banking; experience operating under, or reporting to, a UK/EU regulator strongly preferred given the team's non-US footprint

You are the owner's civil eyes across a portfolio of fast-moving sites: catching design problems before they become field problems, and keeping permits off the critical path.

Site Design Review

Review civil packages across projects - grading and earthwork balance, storm drainage and detention, wet and dry utilities, roadways and access, erosion and sediment control - for constructability, code compliance, and alignment with program standards. Verify civil design supports equipment logistics: heavy-haul routes, crane pads, and laydown.

Permitting & Entitlements Support

Support permitting strategy and submittals with pre-construction and consultants: site development permits, SWPPP/NPDES, floodplain and drainage approvals, utility permits, and DOT access. Track review cycles, drive comment responses, and escalate when agencies threaten the schedule.

Utility & Site Infrastructure Coordination

Construction Support

Respond to civil RFIs and field issues; review submittals, shop drawings, and mix designs; support earthwork QA/QC decisions (compaction, subgrade acceptance, dewatering) with CSA superintendents and project engineers.

Diligence & Early Works

Support site diligence for new projects: grading feasibility, drainage constraints, geotech review coordination, and early-works packages that let construction mobilize before full design completes.

Program Standards

Maintain civil design standards, typical details, and specification updates across the portfolio; capture lessons learned from each site into the next.

Change Identification & Control

Cost & Forecast Integration

Process & Standards

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Superintendent, HV leads high-voltage and substation field execution for a new data center build - owning day-to-day site operations for this scope in a high-stakes, mission-critical environment. Reporting to the Construction Manager and Director, Construction, this role drives schedule, coordinates trades, and enforces safety and quality from mobilization through turnover. Superintendents are the standard on a Hut 8 site: what you walk past, you approve.

Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Substation & Switchyard Construction

Supervise construction of HV substations and switchyards: foundations and steel structures, bus work, breakers, power transformers, disconnects, grounding grids, and control enclosures. Manage major equipment receiving and setting (including oil handling and SF6 procedures) and verify installation against utility and IFC design packages.

Utility Coordination & Outages

Coordinate daily with the serving utility on interconnection scope, clearances, switching orders, and planned outages. Schedule and supervise work inside and adjacent to energized facilities under utility safety rules, hold points, and witness requirements.

Testing & Energization

Sequence and support relay testing, primary injection, doble/megger testing, and end-to-end protection testing with NETA firms and the Protection & Controls Engineer. Own energization readiness: punch completion, test record assembly, safety walkdowns, and utility witness coordination through backfeed and initial energization.

HV Safety Enforcement

Enforce HV-specific safety without exception: minimum approach distances, grounding and bonding, switching and tagging, arc-flash boundaries, and induced-voltage controls. Partner with the HSE Manager on the energization-phase safety plan.

Planning & Contractor Management

Own the HV three-week look-ahead and manage specialty subcontractors and testing firms against schedule and quality commitments. Feed accurate progress and constraints to the Planner/Scheduler - utility windows missed are often windows lost for months.

Documentation & Turnover

Maintain QC documentation, torque and termination records, test records, and as-builts to utility-acceptance standard, and support turnover of HV systems to operations with the CXQC team.

 

ABOUT YOU

-      What we're looking for:

- 7+ years supervising high-voltage substation, switchyard, or transmission construction (69kV-345kV) with a utility contractor, EPC, or utility construction organization.

- Hands-on knowledge of substation construction practice: major equipment setting, bus fabrication, grounding grids, control wiring, and commissioning support.

- Direct experience coordinating utility outages, switching, clearances, and energization - including work in and around energized facilities under utility rules.

- Familiarity with relay and protection testing sequences (NETA, end-to-end) and utility acceptance/witness processes.

- Uncompromising HV safety leadership: switching and tagging, MAD, grounding and bonding; OSHA 30 preferred.

- Experience managing specialty HV subcontractors and NETA testing firms.

- Documentation rigor to utility-acceptance standard.

- Comfortable being the site's HV authority and training adjacent trades on HV hazards.

Own the project's engineering scope end to end. Establish and hold the technical baseline against Hut 8 program standards, the basis of design, and customer requirements. Cross-Discipline Issue Resolution

Drive resolution of cross-discipline conflicts: power and cooling interfaces, space proofing and routing in galleries and white space, structural provisions for equipment, controls integration boundaries, and phasing/sequencing constraints. When disciplines disagree, make the call or escalate with a clear recommendation and the cost/schedule implications of each option.

Design Review Management

Run structured design reviews at each stage gate (30/60/90/IFC), assign reviewers, consolidate comments, and own the comment log to closure. Enforce review quality: constructability, maintainability, code compliance, and alignment with commissioning requirements - not just drafting checks.

Vendor Package & Submittal Oversight

Oversee technical review of major vendor packages (switchgear, generators, UPS, chillers, CDUs, BMS) against specifications. Arbitrate technical exceptions and alternates, and ensure equipment selections hold up against ratings, redundancy, and integration requirements.

Construction & Field Engineering Support

Prioritize and triage engineering support to the field: RFIs, field changes, and design clarifications. Protect the field from slow engineering turnaround by setting response-time expectations and staffing the right discipline against the critical path. Support constructability reviews before packages hit the field.

title: Senior Manager, Strategic Technical Consulting
description:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Technical Consulting is Ramp's post-sales technical delivery team. When a finance org needs Ramp to work the way their business actually runs, this is the team that takes customers through that transformation, from complex accounting issues to integration errors to everything in between.

The Senior Manager, Technical Consulting, Strategic leads the team responsible for Ramp's largest and most strategic accounts. You'll own post-sales technical implementation for this segment end to end — from technical discovery and solution design through go-live, adoption, and expansion — working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Customer Activation team, with whom you'll co-own activation milestones and time-to-value.

Strategic customers arrive with multi-entity structures, legacy ERPs, in-flight finance transformations, procurement and treasury requirements, and executive sponsors who expect a named technical leader in the room. Your team is the last line of technical escalation for these accounts — there is no tier above you.

This role suits an experienced leader who can hold two things at once: the operating rigor to run a delivery function at scale, and the technical credibility to sit across from a Controller or VP of Finance and design the solution live.

  • Lead and grow the Strategic Technical Consulting team — coach senior and principal-level consultants, own hiring, onboarding, performance, and career architecture, and build a bench deep enough to scale with the segment

  • Define the Strategic delivery model — scoping standards, solution design review, rules of engagement with CSM/AM/Activation, staffing and capacity models, and quality bars that hold up under enterprise scrutiny

  • Run the function with operational rigor — forecast capacity, balance workload across accounts, instrument the team with KPIs (time-to-value, go-live on-time rate, escalation volume, adoption and expansion attach), and use the data in coaching and planning

  • Partner cross-functionally at the leadership level — Customer Activation, Strategic CSM and AM, Sales, Product, Engineering, and GTM Ops — to align on roadmap, feedback loops, and segment strategy

  • Turn field insight into product influence — synthesize what Strategic customers actually need, champion it with Product and Engineering, and close the loop back to the field

  • Set precedent where none exists — make sound calls in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, document the reasoning, and teach the team to do the same

  • Deep fluency in ERP and financial systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Oracle, Workday Financials, Microsoft Dynamics), APIs, SSO/HRIS integrations, and core accounting workflows (chart of accounts, subsidiaries, approval hierarchies, month-end close)

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.


About the role

You will own the EEA growth campaign engine, which mainly comprises of 4 types: Affiliate, Listing, Trade & Earn, and New Product Launches. This is both a coordination and execution role. You will be the single accountable owner who turns a campaign concept into a shipped, measured, and reflected-upon outcome by orchestrating creative, media, lifecycle, BD, KOL ops, product marketing, and legal. The number on the campaign is yours. You drive the outcome.

What you will own
  1. Affiliate campaigns: Activation pulses on top of the always-on affiliate channel. Coordinated with BD and BD Operations.
  2. Listing campaigns: New token listing campaigns shipped within 24 hours of listing decisions. Tight loop with Listing PM, legal, comms, BD/KOL Ops, exchange ops.
  3. Trade & Earn campaigns: Volume incentives, leaderboards, zero fee promos. Built around clear unit economics and incrementality, not vanity volume.
  4. Launch campaigns: Product and feature launches. Coordinated with product marketing, product team, social team, and lifecycle team.

What you will do

  1. Translate fuzzy stakeholder asks into clear campaign briefs that creative, paid, and lifecycle can act on without a six-revision loop.
  2. Build and own campaign plans with clear gates, dependencies, owners, and dates. Hold stakeholders accountable when slots slip.
  3. Define success metrics with analytics before launch, not after. Run holdouts where possible. Run reflection sessions within 7 days of campaign close. Publish learnings the team can reuse.
  4. Navigate MiCA and MiFID II constraints with legal. You will not be the lawyer, but you will know enough to flag the risks early and propose alternatives.
  5. Be the connective tissue between EEA Growth and Global Campaigns. Localise global playbooks to EEA markets. Push EEA-originated wins back to global for global execution.

What we are looking for

Must-haves:
  • Four to seven years total experience, two-plus years coordinating end-to-end campaigns at a tier 1 regulated crypto exchange (Binance, Kraken, Bitpanda, Coinbase, or similar). You have shipped at least 10 campaigns with named numbers attached. And you have the receipts.
  • Fluency in English and German, French, or Dutch.
  • Hands-on familiarity with EEA regulator dynamics under MiCA and MiFID II. You have shipped campaigns under regulator review and lived to tell the tales.
  • Strong brief-writing muscle. Strong project management muscle with strong stakeholder management across senior and peer levels.
  • Analytical literacy: you can read a campaign dashboard, spot the wrong attribution, ask the right question of analytics, and present results to leadership.
  • Budget discipline. You understand CAC payback, ROAS, incremental volume, LTV.

Who you are

  • Competitive. You want your campaign on the leaderboard against Global. You want EEA to outperform.
  • Crypto-native. You trade. You have a wallet. You know which tokens listed last week and which exchange ran the best campaign around it. You have opinions.
  • Detail-oriented. You catch the wrong token contract address in a launch comms draft before legal does.
  • Fast. The good campaigns ship within hours of the news, not days.

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About MoonPay

MoonPay is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents.

Recent recognition:


Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 .
2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100
The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running

Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot.


Locations Supported 🌍

  • London, UK

Relocation available: No

Work pattern: Hybrid: our teams meets in the office ~1-2 days a week

About the Opportunity

Every transaction we process requires a real-time decision. Declining a legitimate transaction leaves a customer stuck at the point of purchase, while approving a fraudulent one carries a direct cost.

This role owns the decisioning system and underlying platform. From the serving path and feature infrastructure to the underlying models and the machinery required to make safe, live updates. You will continuously improve the platform and our day to day workflows, rather than treating these as secondary projects.

As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will hold a hands-on technical position. You will be part of a team that builds, ships, and maintains the entire machine learning lifecycle.

Our main focus is fraud detection and prevention, an adversarial domain where opponents constantly adapt and feedback arrives in the form of financial impact. Alongside, this we build broader capabilities to enable machine learning across Moonpay.

Lead through ambiguity

  • Turn vague problems into well-defined solutions and bring people with you.

  • Set the technical bar through rigorous reviews, clear standards, and lasting engineering habits.

Build and scale the platform

  • Develop feature infrastructure across batch, near-real-time, and in-request paths, managing specific freshness budgets for each.

  • Maintain alignment between training and serving to ensure models behave in production exactly as they did offline.

  • Integrate feedback loops to capture every decision and its outcome, including blocked transactions where results are counterfactual.

  • Scale the platform as volume and model complexity grow, ensuring operational load remains manageable.

Decide in real time

  • Own the services that score transactions in-flight, inside a hard latency budget

  • Design the degraded paths: what we answer when the model can't, and who agreed that policy

Ship safely, continuously

  • Mature the replay, shadow and staged-rollout tooling until changing a live model is routine and reversible

  • Own models across their lifecycle, from training through to retirement, and catch decay long before losses confirm it

About You

Must-have experience and skills

  • Real-time serving. You have built and operated high-availability services that execute within strict latency budgets on critical paths, and you’ve designed robust fallback mechanisms

  • Systems thinking. You view the architecture holistically: identifying failure points, managing graceful degradation, and ensuring the system remains responsive even when dependencies fail. You build the feedback loops that allow a system to learn from its own decisions.

  • Engineering craft. You write code other people are happy to inherit — tested, typed, and correct when events arrive twice, late, or out of order. Adding the next feature to something you built is fast and painless.

  • Pipelines in production. You have owned feature or data pipelines end-to-end, including troubleshooting cases where offline and production metrics diverged and resolving the underlying discrepancies.

  • Ambiguity and influence. You've taken a problem nobody had scoped and turned it into work that shipped, and raised the level of the engineers around you while doing it.

Nice-to-have experience

  • Decision explainability. You've built systems where the reason for a decision mattered as much as the decision: audit trails, per-layer attribution, llm-driven analyses, or defending a model's behaviour to a non-technical audience.

  • Anomaly detection. You have developed systems to detect novel attack patterns and emerging abuse without existing labels, identifying suspicious behavior relative to historical baselines.

  • Familiarity with our stack: GCP, BigQuery, Bigtable, Memorystore, Vertex AI, Kubernetes.

Benefits & Perks 💡

  • 💰 Competitive salary package

  • 🤝 Equity package: financial freedom starts with our employees, so all employees have ownership at MoonPay

  • 📈 Pay-for-performance equity bonus: those who drive outsized outcomes receive outsized rewards

  • 🚀 Moonshot award: we honor exceptional impact. 10 employees twice a year, each earning a $250,000 equity grant

  • 📊Pension: employer contributions from day one

  • 🎁Employee referral program: refer great people, earn 10K in USDC

  • 🏝 Flexible Time Off: choose when to work and when to switch off

  • 🎂 Birthday leave: take the day off to celebrate you

  • 🍼 Enhanced parental leave: more time with family, no second thought

  • 🌍 Hybrid working schedule: work fully remotely or from your nearest Moonbase

  • 🚆 Commuter benefits: public transport to and from the office

  • 🩺 Private healthcare benefits: to protect you and your loved ones

  • 🧘 Wellhub wellness membership: access to gyms, studios, classes, and wellness apps in one membership

  • 🤖 Unlimited enterprise access to the latest AI tools: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and whatever's next

  • 🍱 Lunch credit: meals covered on the days you're in the office

  • 🪑 Home office setup allowance: build the home office of your dreams

  • 👛 Remote working allowance: those working fully remotely get a little extra for utilities

  • 🌕 Monthly product budget and zero-fee crypto transactions

  • 📚 $1,000 Annual training budget: we support your learning journey

  • 🎯 High Potential Program: structured development, mentorship, and stretch opportunities

  • ✈️ Regular remote company offsites: high-impact in-person sessions and hackathons

  • 🚲 (Ireland) Cycle to Work scheme: tax-efficient bike, gear, and safety kit

  • 🔌 (UK) EV Salary Sacrifice: lease an electric vehicle through pre-tax salary

title: Business Development Lead
description:
Location: Remote (U.S.) — Washington, D.C. preferred

Employment Type: Full time

Location Type: Remote

About Us

Swan delivers the future of defense and industry through scalable autonomous products. Swan is backed by leading defense VCs, including a16z's American Dynamism fund.

About the Team

The Business Development (BD) team at Swan is responsible for identifying, shaping, capturing, and growing opportunities across our government customer base. BD team members serve as the bridge between the customers and the company. They are responsible for translating mission needs and user feedback internally, while acting as Swan's ambassador externally to clients, partners, and the broader defense and national security community. The team partners closely with strategy, corporate development, engineering, operations, and capture functions to ensure Swan's products consistently meet mission demands.

About the Role

Swan is looking for a high-initiative, collaborative Business Development (BD) Lead to own growth across our priority government and defense customer base. This is a highly strategic, externally-facing role responsible for the full lifecycle of opportunity development. This is a foundational hire in the Strategy and Growth organization: you will shape how Swan approaches government growth and will have real ownership and autonomy to move fast.

What You'll Do

Identify and capture opportunities. Find, pursue, and close business within your assigned customer set. Build a deep understanding of the existing and prospective customer base, current and planned programmatic/technical roadmaps, budget and acquisition cycles, and the competitive landscape. Use this expertise to inform capture strategies, revenue forecasts, and technology development plans.

Develop capture strategies. Build cohesive business plans and execution models that outline acquisition pathways, align to investment strategy, and drive toward program-of-record execution. Engage key stakeholders to shape requirements, identify and secure relevant funding, and develop compelling win themes and teaming/supplier strategies for competitive captures.

Conduct market and competitive research. Continuously monitor opportunities (e.g., SAM.gov, subscription intelligence services, on-the-ground networking), track emerging programs, and analyze the competitive landscape to inform opportunity qualification, teaming decisions, narrative development, and product roadmap prioritization.

Drive product development and program transition. Translate customer problem sets back into Swan's engineering organization, participate in engineering planning sessions, identify key milestones, and proactively communicate across the company. Your read on client needs will directly inform product roadmap decisions.

Own proposal and content development. Lead or significantly contribute to proposals, white papers, and market research responses. Translate customer priorities into clear, concise, and compelling narratives that speak directly to stated and unstated needs.

Grow existing business. Beyond new capture, represent the full breadth of Swan's offering to current clients. Partner with execution teams and product engineers to expand current programs and surface new opportunities within existing relationships.

Represent Swan externally. Plan and lead customer meetings, industry days, conferences, and trade shows. Communicate Swan's mission, approach, and competitive edge to a broad range of audiences.

Manage pipeline and forecasting. Own qualification, cultivation, and capture of opportunities in partnership with growth, engineering, and operations teammates; track pipeline and consistently deliver against bookings and growth targets using CRM tooling.

Required Qualifications

● 5+ years of experience in business development, capture, sales, or program strategy supporting or serving U.S. military, government, or allied defense organizations (or equivalent commercial/DoD capture experience).

● Demonstrated track record building, executing, and winning business capture strategies, with a proven history of closing opportunities.

● Strong understanding of U.S. Government (or relevant allied) procurement processes, acquisition pathways, and the full capture lifecycle.

● Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience briefing senior executives, government officials, and customers.

● Comfort operating with high ownership in an ambiguous, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

● Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (engineering, business, political science, international relations, or equivalent experience).

● Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance; active Secret clearance strongly preferred.

● Willingness to travel 50–75%.

Preferred Qualifications

● Established relationships across relevant government stakeholders, program offices, and mission partners..

● Experience with non-traditional acquisition pathways (OTAs, BAAs/CSOs, rapid prototyping/fielding) and commercial-style contracting.

● Prior U.S. military, government, or relevant allied-nation government experience.

● Domain experience relevant to Swan's product line (e.g., autonomy, robotics, sensors, unmanned systems, or similar).

● Experience with FMS/DCS or direct international sales processes, including licensing and releasability.

● Technical background or degree (engineering, computer science, physics, or related) is a plus.

● Currently holds an active U.S. Secret clearance (or higher) is a plus.

What We Offer

Swan is a fast-paced, innovative, and collaborative startup environment. We offer a top-notch benefits package, including:

- Top-tier health, dental, vision, short-/long-term disability, and life insurance, with full employee coverage and partial coverage for dependents

- Flexible/reasonable vacation and sick leave

- 401(k) plans, FSA, HSA, and commuter benefits

Swan is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. title: Proposal Writer / Capture Manager
description:
Proposal Writer / Capture & Growth Manager

Growth / Business Development · Remote (U.S.), Washington, DC or San Francisco preferred · Full time

About Us

Swan delivers the future of defense and industry through scalable autonomous products. Swan is backed by leading defense VCs including a16z’s American Dynamism fund.

Role Overview

Swan is seeking a Proposal Writer / Capture & Growth Manager to sit at the heart of our growth engine. In this role you are, first and foremost, a writer. You will craft the compelling technical narratives and documents that win new business, while also owning the capture process that shapes and qualifies the opportunities behind them. You will partner across business development, engineering, program management, finance, legal, and the executive team to translate Swan’s autonomy and hardware capabilities into mission-focused proposals that close deals. This is a build-it role. You will create structure where none exists, run the proposal operation end to end, keep the pipeline and internal initiatives moving, and navigate the fast-paced, high-stakes environment of a hyper-growth defense-technology startup. You thrive on short timelines, understand the U.S. Government acquisition process, and know how to move an opportunity from first contact to signed contract. This position supports DoD, OTA, SBIR/STTR, DIU, and other federal technology pursuits.

Key Responsibilities

Proposal Writing and Technical Content

• Serve as primary author for technical and management proposal volumes, including technical and management approaches, past performance narratives, staffing approaches, Quality Management Plans, Risk Management Plans, Statements of Work, CDRLs, and supporting technical documentation.

• Produce supporting artifacts including white papers, quad charts, one-pagers, and capability statements.

• Translate complex engineering concepts into clear, persuasive, evaluator-focused proposal language, working closely with Swan’s engineering team to accurately represent our technology to customers.

• Maintain consistency in terminology, voice, and tone across every volume and pursuit.

• Refine drafts to improve clarity, flow, and persuasiveness, and support other authors through review cycles.

• Build and curate a reusable content library of past performance, technical boilerplate, briefs, and graphics for use across the business.

Proposal Management and Process

• Own end-to-end proposal development, leading responses to Government and customer RFPs, RFIs, RFQs, white papers, SBIR/STTR, and OTA solicitations from kickoff through submission.

• Develop compliance matrices, build proposal schedules, track writing assignments, coordinate SMEs, manage action items, and maintain document versions.

• Run color team reviews (pink, red, gold), incorporate executive feedback, and prepare final production packages.

• Continuously improve the proposal process to ensure on-time, fully compliant, high-quality submissions across multiple concurrent pursuits.

• Manage proposal content on unclassified and, as needed, classified systems, ensuring security compliance and proper marking and handling throughout.

Capture and Pipeline

• Drive capture management for priority pursuits: qualify opportunities, build and execute capture plans, shape requirements with customers, and improve probability of win (pWin) through disciplined gate reviews.

• Build and maintain the opportunity pipeline; monitor SAM.gov, DIU, AFWERX/SpaceWERX, SOCOM, SBIR/STTR, and other channels; flag and qualify new opportunities for leadership.

• Support go/no-go reviews, conduct opportunity research, organize customer intelligence, and maintain CRM data.

• Prepare customer briefing materials and support commercialization planning.

• Lead teaming and partner strategy with primes, subcontractors, and non-traditional partners.

• Develop and maintain strategic pricing and Basis of Estimate in partnership with finance; support cost and price volumes.

Project and Program Coordination

• Develop executive briefings, maintain project documentation, support risk tracking, and create status reports.

• Improve internal workflows so multiple company initiatives stay organized and moving forward.

AI-Enabled Proposal Development

• Develop internal prompt libraries and organize proposal knowledge repositories.

• Maintain a technically credible writing style while avoiding generic AI-generated language.

Qualifications and Skills

• 5+ years of experience in federal proposal writing, capture management, technical writing, or business development within government, defense contracting, or GovCon.

• Exceptional writing and editing skills, with a demonstrated ability to generate large, compliant documents on short timelines.

• Working knowledge of the U.S. Government solicitation and acquisition process (RFPs, RFIs, RFQs, white papers, SBIR/STTR, OTAs).

• Experience owning or driving capture plans, gate and color team reviews, and win strategy (Shipley or a comparable methodology).

• Proven ability to build process where none exists and to operate independently in a fast-paced, hyper-growth environment.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, able to extract technical content from engineers and translate it clearly for non-technical customers.

• Strong organizational and project management ability, with comfort managing competing priorities and overlapping proposal schedules.• Familiarity with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and Figma, and comfort using AI tools to improve writing and productivity.

• Structured, systems-oriented thinker who is deadline-driven, coachable, and comfortable receiving heavy feedback on drafts.

Preferred Qualifications
